Builders correctly committed test+code together rather than red test-only commits; the method's test-then-feat series order conflicts with every-commit-green and should say so. result: challenge run, 12 contexts / 24 cards, Sonnet scouts+critic+builders at 4/8/12 width as a resource bench: 24/24 landed, 12 flawless (11 strict), 3 integration gates green
comment: Run doubled as a hardware bench on a 20-core Arm box, so widths were deliberately past the skill default. Lessons: (1) Test-first discipline decays under CPU starvation - flawless share 3/4 at 4-way, 3/8 at 8-way, 6/12 at 12-way; builders wrote cases after code when gates were slow. Builder brief should make red-before a hard stop, not a report field. (2) A builder that launches its full suite in the background and ends its turn is never woken; it sat 1h45 uncommitted. Brief should require foreground gate runs. (3) Builder self-reported started/finished timestamps were invented; use harness duration. (4) Whole-tree gates inside a shared checkout at 8+ builders are noisy (sibling in-flight files); only the post-wave integration gate is a verdict, which challenge.md already says. (5) Throughput peaks around 4 full-suite builders on 20 cores (0.25 vs 0.19 vs 0.17 builds/min).
